name: Fix a broken Falco rule
objective: CKS › Runtime Security (the behavioral-detection slice the exam weights heavily). Drill every Falco corner harder than the exam: deploy the DaemonSet with the right driver, confirm the per-node rollout, author a custom rule with exact macros, shape its output fields, reuse a list + macro, tune with an exception, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix of a broken rule. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a broken custom rule
questions.teach:
Falco **refuses to load** a rules file with an error, so a single bad rule silences the whole file. Common faults: a condition referencing an **undefined macro** (a typo), or a stray `enabled: false`. Falco surfaces these as load errors — in the exam you'd read them from the pod logs, then fix the YAML.

**Gotcha:** an undefined-macro typo makes Falco reject the file; fix the reference to the real macro and re-enable the rule.
questions.prompt:
The ConfigMap `falco-custom-rules` in namespace `falco` holds a rule `Detect package mgmt in container` (key `custom_rules.yaml`) that is **broken** two ways: its condition references an undefined macro `spawned_proces` (a typo for `spawned_process`), and the rule carries `enabled: false`. Fix the ConfigMap so the rule's condition uses `spawned_process` and the rule is enabled. Do not delete the ConfigMap or the rule.

Target: in `falco-custom-rules`/`custom_rules.yaml`, the rule references `spawned_process` (no `spawned_proces` typo) and has no `enabled: false`.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n falco get cm falco-custom-rules -o jsonpath='{.data.custom_rules\.yaml}'` to read it. Fix the typo `spawned_proces` → `spawned_process` and remove/flip the `enabled: false` line, then `kubectl -n falco apply`/`edit` the ConfigMap.
questions.solution:
# Read it:
kubectl -n falco get cm falco-custom-rules -o jsonpath='{.data.custom_rules\.yaml}'
# Fix: 'spawned_proces' -> 'spawned_process', drop 'enabled: false'. e.g. edit:
kubectl -n falco edit configmap falco-custom-rules
# resulting rule condition: spawned_process and container, no 'enabled: false'

verification.description: broken rule fixed: condition uses spawned_process (no typo) and rule enabled

questions.eli5:
Falco reads its rules like a strict proofreader: if **one** rule in a file has a mistake, it won't just skip that rule — it **refuses to load the entire file**. So a single typo can switch off *all* your detection at once, even though nothing looks obviously broken.

Here the rule `Detect package mgmt in container` is broken **two** ways:

1. Its condition names a macro `spawned_proces` — but that macro doesn't exist; it's a **typo** for the real `spawned_process`. Falco sees "you're referring to something I've never heard of" and rejects the file.
2. The rule also has `enabled: false` stuck on it — so even after you fix the typo, the rule would still be switched off.

Your job is detective work: in real life you'd read the error straight out of Falco's **pod logs** ("undefined macro spawned_proces"), then go fix the YAML — correct the spelling and remove the `enabled: false`. You must *fix*, not delete: keep the ConfigMap and the rule.

**Watch out for:**

- **One bad rule breaks the whole file** — Falco won't load any of it until the error is gone.
- The fault here is an **undefined macro** (`spawned_proces`): fix it to the real name `spawned_process`.
- There are **two** problems — the typo *and* `enabled: false`. Fixing only one still leaves the rule dead.
- **Read the pod logs** to find load errors: `kubectl -n falco logs ds/falco` shows the exact complaint.
- Do **not** delete the ConfigMap or the rule — edit it in place.
- After editing, reload Falco (`rollout restart ds/falco`) so it re-reads the corrected file.
questions.deepDive:
## Diagnosing & fixing a broken Falco rule — full rundown

### Mental model
Falco loads rules files **atomically per file**: it parses and validates the whole file, and if **any** item fails (undefined macro/list, bad YAML, invalid priority), it **rejects the entire file** and logs an error. The DaemonSet keeps running on previously-good rules (or none), so detection can silently degrade. Troubleshooting is a loop: **read the load error → fix the YAML → reload → confirm the rule loaded**.

### The two classic faults in this scenario
| Fault | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Condition references an **undefined macro** (`spawned_proces`, a typo) | load error "undefined macro 'spawned_proces'"; file not loaded | correct to the real macro `spawned_process` |
| Rule carries **`enabled: false`** | file may load, but the rule never fires | remove the line (or set `true`) |

Both must be fixed; fixing only the typo leaves a loaded-but-disabled rule, fixing only `enabled` leaves an unloadable file.

### Step 1 — read the error
```bash
# the actual load error Falco prints at startup / reload
kubectl -n falco logs ds/falco | grep -iE 'error|invalid|undefined|load'
# e.g. "Runtime error: ... undefined macro 'spawned_proces' ..."
```

### Step 2 — read the broken rule
```bash
kubectl -n falco get cm falco-custom-rules \
  -o jsonpath='{.data.custom_rules\.yaml}'
```
Look for the typo in `condition:` and any `enabled: false`.

### Step 3 — fix the ConfigMap in place
```bash
kubectl -n falco edit configmap falco-custom-rules
```
Correct `spawned_proces` → `spawned_process`, delete the `enabled: false` line. Resulting rule:
```yaml
- rule: Detect package mgmt in container
  desc: package management launched in a container
  condition: spawned_process and container     # fixed macro, no typo
  output: "pkg mgmt in container (cmd=%proc.cmdline container=%container.id)"
  priority: WARNING
  # no 'enabled: false'
```
Do **not** delete the ConfigMap or the rule — the task requires the rule to survive, just corrected.

### Step 4 — reload and confirm
```bash
kubectl -n falco rollout restart ds/falco
kubectl -n falco rollout status  ds/falco
kubectl -n falco logs ds/falco | grep -i 'rules.*loaded\|error'   # clean load, no errors
```

### Validate offline first (optional but exam-fast)
```bash
# inside a falco pod or with the binary
falco --validate /etc/falco/custom_rules.yaml   # prints the exact parse/undefined error
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **One error fails the whole file** — Falco won't partially load; detection is fully off until fixed.
- **Undefined macro/list = load error**, not a silent skip. A single-character typo (`spawned_proces`) is enough.
- **`enabled: false` is independent of the parse error** — a file can load fine yet the rule still won't fire. Check both.
- **Diagnose from logs** (`kubectl -n falco logs ds/falco`) — the message names the offending macro and file.
- **Edit, don't delete.** Keep the ConfigMap and the rule; only correct them.
- **Reload after editing** — ConfigMap changes aren't picked up until the DaemonSet restarts (or hot-reload fires).
- Escape the dotted key in jsonpath: `.data.custom_rules\.yaml`.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl -n falco logs ds/falco | grep -i undefined          # find the typo'd macro
kubectl -n falco get cm falco-custom-rules -o jsonpath='{.data.custom_rules\.yaml}'
kubectl -n falco edit configmap falco-custom-rules          # fix spawned_proces -> spawned_process; drop enabled:false
kubectl -n falco rollout restart ds/falco                   # reload
```
